edges.relationship: Examines changing grounds for the moral and epistemic authority of scientists.
edges.evidence_note: Own interview distinguishes virtue attributed to individuals and institutions; does not deny knowledge of nature.

edges.relationship: Questions simple academic/industrial contrasts and studies credibility under entrepreneurial uncertainty.
edges.evidence_note: Own interview treats commercial science as a historically specific social setting; commercial profit is not asserted to explain every scientific judgment.

edges.relationship: Connects aristocratic wealth and power to urban development as well as rural landholding.
edges.evidence_note: Own interview describes Calthorpe ground rents and Edgbaston, motivating a broader social history of aristocracy.

edges.relationship: Treats biography as a balance of private/public life, evidence, proportion and competing historical judgments.
edges.evidence_note: Own interview’s ODNB and Thatcher answers explain the method; his acknowledgment of underrepresented women/businesspeople concerns an editorial programme, not sole authorship of dictionary lives.

edges.relationship: Interprets French national belonging as historically produced through uneven rural integration.
edges.evidence_note: Agulhon’s substantive review843reports the thesis and questions its political periodization; not automatic adoption of the modernization label.

edges.relationship: Combines markets and transport with schools and conscription as mechanisms of rural transformation.
edges.evidence_note: Agulhon credits the plural account while asking whether deliberate state integration is given too much weight; the critique remains explicit.

edges.relationship: Distinguishes emotional standards from emotional experience while investigating relations between them.
edges.evidence_note: Own2010answer262insists cultural prescription does not necessarily describe experience; joint earlier concept credit to Carol Z.Stearns retained.

edges.relationship: Connects emotions to social action, work and family without discarding rational interests.
edges.evidence_note: Own2010answer263makes emotional cues a component of social history, rather than a replacement for the history of interests.

edges.relationship: Studies European political self-understanding through ideas of empire and relations with peoples outside Europe.
edges.evidence_note: Own interview relates Hispanic/Amerindian encounters to European categories, not simply Spanish national ideas.

edges.relationship: Connects projects of European unity with imperial experience and changing international arrangements.
edges.evidence_note: Own interview distinguishes Europe’s aggregate of states from empire, while acknowledging imperial preservation as part of the history. His cosmopolitan-progressive evaluation remains his position.

edges.relationship: Documents women’s public political activity through associations, protests and street participation despite exclusion from suffrage.
edges.evidence_note: Fraser61explicitly attributes these historical findings to Ryan; different classes/ethnicities use different routes, not one universal female experience.

edges.relationship: Provides historical evidence against equating public politics with a single bourgeois public sphere.
edges.evidence_note: Fraser61uses Ryan’s findings to critique Habermas; this is Fraser’s mediated deployment of Ryan, not evidence Ryan adopted every element of Fraser’s theory or belonged to the Frankfurt School.

edges.relationship: Reinterprets Prohibition as consequential state-building and political realignment.
edges.evidence_note: Own interview describes expanded enforcement while expressly denying it alone caused the later carceral state.

edges.relationship: Shows Prohibition enforcement becoming an instrument of white Protestant supremacy and unequal coercion.
edges.evidence_note: Own Herrin answer identifies Klan recruitment and selective action against ethnic/religious targets; one locality is not presented as every locality.

edges.relationship: Studies nativism and ethnic relations as central to American nationalism and pluralism.
edges.evidence_note: Dorothy Ross’s substantive retrospective describes the project and later revisions; the nativism interpretation is not an endorsement of exclusion.

edges.relationship: Criticizes consensus narratives that flatten conflict and diversity in American history.
edges.evidence_note: Existing complete1959primary reading, with original qualifications preserved; does not imply a wholesale return to older economic dualisms.

edges.relationship: Makes changing collective fears and searches for security objects of historical inquiry.
edges.evidence_note: Paillard’s substantive introduction and Delumeau’s1991research inset support this; no claim that all fear has one unchanging religious cause.

edges.relationship: Warns that psychological interpretations of the past must respect documentary limits and disciplinary methods.
edges.evidence_note: Paillard17reports Delumeau’s position, including caution about sparse or contested evidence and Freud’s critique of religion; this is a specific methodological criticism, not rejection of all psychology.
